name: Public Comment Templates
description: Pre-built templates for public comment at government meetings

templates.name: Support an Item
templates.description: Use when you want to speak in favor of something
templates.template:
Good evening, Council President and members of Council. My name is [NAME] and I live at [ADDRESS] in [MUNICIPALITY].

I'm here tonight to speak IN SUPPORT of [AGENDA ITEM].

[MAIN REASON - 2-3 sentences explaining why you support it]

[PERSONAL CONNECTION - How does this affect you or your community?]

[SUPPORTING POINT - Additional reason or data]

I urge Council to vote YES on this item. Thank you for your time and service.
tips: Lead with your strongest reason
Personal stories are powerful
Be specific about the item number
End with a clear 'vote yes' ask

templates.name: Oppose an Item
templates.description: Use when you want to speak against something
templates.template:
Good evening, Council President and members of Council. My name is [NAME] and I live at [ADDRESS] in [MUNICIPALITY].

I'm here tonight to speak IN OPPOSITION to [AGENDA ITEM].

[MAIN CONCERN - 2-3 sentences explaining your opposition]

[IMPACT - How will this negatively affect you or the community?]

[ALTERNATIVE - What would you suggest instead?]

I urge Council to vote NO on this item, or to table it for further consideration. Thank you.
tips: Stay calm and factual, not emotional
Propose alternatives if possible
Acknowledge any valid points on the other side
Ask to table if more information is needed

templates.name: Ask Questions
templates.description: Use when you need information or clarification
templates.template:
Good evening, Council President and members of Council. My name is [NAME] from [MUNICIPALITY].

I have questions about [AGENDA ITEM] that I hope can be addressed:

1. [SPECIFIC QUESTION #1]

2. [SPECIFIC QUESTION #2]

I believe these answers are important for the public to understand before a vote is taken. Thank you.
tips: Keep questions clear and answerable
Limit to 2-3 questions maximum
Officials may not answer during public comment
Follow up with written request if not answered

templates.name: Raise a Concern
templates.description: Use when bringing an issue to Council's attention
templates.template:
Good evening. My name is [NAME] and I'm a resident of [MUNICIPALITY].

I want to bring to Council's attention a concern regarding [TOPIC].

[DESCRIBE THE ISSUE - What's happening? Where? How long?]

[IMPACT - How is this affecting residents?]

[REQUEST - What action are you asking Council to take?]

I would appreciate a response or follow-up on this matter. Thank you.
tips: Be specific about locations and timeframes
Suggest which department might handle it
Ask for follow-up (email, phone call)
Bring documentation if you have it

templates.name: Budget Comment
templates.description: Use during budget hearings or to discuss spending
templates.template:
Good evening, Council President. My name is [NAME] from [MUNICIPALITY].

I'm here to comment on the proposed [YEAR] budget, specifically regarding [DEPARTMENT OR LINE ITEM].

[YOUR POSITION - Support increase? Oppose cut? Request addition?]

[JUSTIFICATION - Why is this funding important?]

[DATA OR EXAMPLES - If available]

I ask that Council consider this as you finalize the budget. Thank you for your fiscal stewardship.
tips: Reference specific line items or departments
Quantify impact if possible
Acknowledge budget constraints
Prioritize - what's most important?

templates.name: Thank/Recognize
templates.description: Use to thank officials or recognize good work
templates.template:
Good evening. My name is [NAME] from [MUNICIPALITY].

I'm here tonight not with a complaint, but to thank [OFFICIAL/DEPARTMENT] for [SPECIFIC ACTION OR SERVICE].

[DESCRIBE WHAT HAPPENED - What did they do well?]

[IMPACT - How did it help you or the community?]

It's important to recognize good work when we see it. Thank you for your service.
tips: Be specific about what you're thanking them for
Positive feedback is rare and appreciated
Copy in supervisors/department heads
Consider also sending written thank you

templates.name: Development/Zoning
templates.description: Use for warehouse, construction, or zoning concerns
templates.template:
Good evening, Council President. My name is [NAME] and I live at [ADDRESS], approximately [DISTANCE] from the proposed [PROJECT NAME].

I'm here to express my [SUPPORT/CONCERN] regarding this development.

[SPECIFIC CONCERNS - Traffic, noise, environmental, property values?]

[QUESTIONS - What studies have been done? What mitigation is proposed?]

[REQUEST - What conditions or modifications would you want?]

I ask that Council carefully consider the impact on existing residents. Thank you.
tips: Establish your proximity to the project
Focus on factual impacts, not emotions
Request specific conditions if supportable
Attend planning commission meetings too

templates.name: Transparency/Accountability
templates.description: Use to request better government transparency
templates.template:
Good evening. My name is [NAME] from [MUNICIPALITY].

I'm here to address a transparency concern regarding [TOPIC].

[WHAT INFORMATION IS NEEDED - What's missing or unclear?]

[WHY IT MATTERS - Why should the public have this information?]

[REQUEST - Post online? Provide reports? Hold hearing?]

Transparency builds public trust. I ask Council to ensure this information is made accessible. Thank you.
tips: Reference specific documents or data
Cite Right-to-Know Law if applicable
Suggest how information could be shared
Be persistent but respectful

generalTips: Sign up for public comment (if required)
State your name and address clearly for the record
Address the Chair/President, not individual members
Stay within time limit - you'll be cut off
Be respectful even if you disagree strongly
Bring copies of any documents you reference
Stay for the vote if possible
whatNotToDo: Applause, booing, or outbursts from audience
Reading from a long document verbatim
